title: Sell My House Fast in Hampton, VA | We Buy Houses for Cash
description: We buy houses in Hampton, VA for cash, as-is. Local REALTOR® Chris Jenkins makes honest, no-obligation offers with no repairs, showings or listing fees.
h1: Sell My House Fast in Hampton, VA: We Buy Houses for Cash
lede: If you need to sell a Hampton house quickly, whether it is a rental, an inherited home or just more work than you want, I will make you a straight cash offer and say so honestly when listing would pay more.
tldr: Chris Jenkins, a licensed Virginia REALTOR® with Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate – Native American Group, buys Hampton houses for cash, as-is. Each offer is built from nearby closed sales and the work the house needs.

sections.h2: Cash Home Buyer in Hampton: How It Works
sections.html:
Hampton is one of the oldest English-speaking communities in the country, and its housing stock shows it: mid-century neighborhoods, waterfront streets and newer pockets all sit within a few miles. That mix is why a Hampton offer has to come from sales near your address.

I have not published Hampton neighborhood statistics on this site yet, so I will not quote a median here. Send me your address and I will pull the closed sales nearby from REIN MLS and show you the numbers behind any offer.

Hampton set up rental inspection districts by ordinance in October 2013, according to the ACLU of Virginia, and the city also adopted new short-term rental rules reported by WHRO.

Virginia law allows localities to create rental inspection districts. If you own a Hampton rental and want out of inspections, repairs or turnover, tell me about the lease, the rent and the condition. Please confirm current city requirements for your address.

sections.h2: Langley Air Force Base and Military Sellers in Hampton
sections.html: Langley Air Force Base is part of Joint Base Langley-Eustis, and many Hampton homeowners are on orders. If you have a report date, tell me and I will say honestly whether a direct sale, a listing or a rental fits. Read VA loan entitlement and PCS moves first.

sections.h2: Inherited and Waterfront Homes in Hampton
sections.html:
Probate is handled by the circuit court clerk in the city where the person lived, which for a Hampton resident is the Hampton Circuit Court clerk. Read how to sell an inherited house.

Much of Hampton is near water. Selling as-is does not remove disclosure duties, including for a known repetitive risk loss structure. See the statute and why elevation certificates matter.

faqs: Do you buy Hampton houses in any condition?
I look at houses in many conditions, including ones that need major work. Tell me what you know and I will give an honest answer.
How do you decide what to offer on a Hampton house?

I pull closed sales near your address from REIN MLS, subtract the repairs and updates the house needs and the cost and risk of holding and reselling it, and show you the math. A cash offer is generally below what a fully prepared house could get on the open market.
I own a rental in a Hampton inspection district. Can I still sell?
Yes. Tell me about the property, the lease and any open inspection items, and we can work out the cleanest way to sell. Confirm current city requirements for your address.
I have PCS orders from Langley. How fast can this move?
As fast as clear title and paperwork allow. Give me your report date and what is owed on the house and I will say honestly whether it works.
Who can sell an inherited Hampton house?
Generally the executor or administrator, after qualifying with the circuit court clerk. A Virginia attorney can confirm the steps for your estate.
Can I sell my Hampton house before foreclosure?
In most cases you can sell until the foreclosure sale takes place. Read this guide and talk with a Virginia attorney or housing counselor.
Do I pay a Realtor commission if I sell to you in Hampton?

On a direct sale there is no listing commission. Closing costs and taxes still apply, and I will go over them with you before you decide. I will also tell you honestly what listing would likely net you.
How do I know this is not a scam?
Ask who the actual buyer is, ask for proof of funds, get the offer in writing, close through a title company or attorney and check any license with the Virginia DPOR.
